posts.title: Judging Evil Favorably 2
posts.body: Rabbainu in Likutay Moharan Tora 55 explains that H"Y judges the wicked favorably in order to save the righteous from the evil eye of the wicked. By placing His hand on the harsh judgement that should have been given, holding it back by judging them favorably, the eyes of the wicked are dimmed and they can not see properly, and thus the righteous are saved.This is mamash the concept found by shochad, bribery. The Tora says do not take bribery for it blinds the eyes, our Sages taught that even to take bribery that was given to judge correctly is forbidden. Bribery is given to promote one's cause, and results in blinding the eyes of the judge. Judging someone favorably, also a type of bribery, is given to promote their cause and saves one from their eyes!Na Nach Nachmu Nachman Meuman!

posts.title: Judging the Evil Favoribly
posts.body: Rabbainu says in Likutay Moharan Tora 55, that in order for the righteous to be saved from the evil eye of the wicked they must judge the wicked favoribly, and for this reason even H"Y judges them favorably. The way I understand this, is that as much as a person decides and credits the force and power of evil, this itself gives the evil the recognition and power to prevail. However when a person decides that something isn't really evil then that force is dissipated, after all it isn't so terrible as it seemed.... E.g. a kid that doesn't wake up every night for chatzos and doesn't do hisbodidus every day C"V, if we look at him as evil, then we are saying that evil is prevailing and thus the kid will actually be empowered with evil C"V. However if we look at the kid as a tinok shinishba bain halitvishe (a baby that was taken captive by the orthodox scholars) etc. the kid still has not fallen completely into their side. H"Y should help us see Him and His goodness wherever we look and in whatever we think about or contemplate, in the zichus (merit) and power of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman Meuman!

posts.title: The Passing on of R' Noach Weinberg
posts.body: This morning my grandfather's younger brother, R' Noach Weinberg the rosh yeshiva of Aish Hatora passed away.     My grandfather used to tell everyone about his father who was a recognised mohel who circumcised 500 babes, and upon occasion saw babies who were born somewhat circumcised, but never did he (my grandfather's father) see any baby born completely circumcised like R' Noach (there were hand motions that went along with this recounting...). Rabbainu says that a person who is born circumcised has pure 'dimyonos' - meanderings of the mind, this is something extremely special, an aspect of tikun habris and tzidkus.    R' Noach would tell people that the world is suffering a worse holocaust today than it did 70 years ago, we are losing so many more souls to the klipa. R' Noach responded with first aid as best as he could give it, doing his utmost to keep Jews Jewish and regain the lost souls. It is very unfortunate that people think that they are the first people that realize that the Jews need help, as if there aren't and weren't huge tzadikim, who cared alot more than us for Israel, and know and knew alot better than we can ever know what is needed for the Jews and the whole world. It is a tremendous shame that people do not humble themselves to Rabbainu and follow his holy teachings and spread them. It is for this reason we are in exile still.    B"H we have Na Nach Nachmu Nachman Meuman, we can do a lot more than first aid, we can rectify the situation completely B"H, and we don't have to rely on our own puny efforts, because B"H we have the broad shoulders of Rabbainu to rely upon.    May H"Y comfort all of Israel with the holy and joyous song Na Nach Nachmu Nachman Meuman.

posts.title: The Head, Hands, and Feet of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman Meuman!
posts.body: It says in Hoshaya (11:3) ואנכי תרגלתי לאפרים קחם על זרועתיו ולא ידעו כי רפאתים Rash'i there and in Parshas Vayichi brings from our Sages that this is referring to when Yosef brought his two sons Efraim and Menashe to get a blessing from Yakov, and Yakov saw different evil people that would be born from them in future generations and as a result the divine spirit left Yakov and he asked Yosef, who are these, Yosef supplicated for mercy and the Divine spirit rested on Yakov and he blessed them (amazingly right after I posted this, I sat down to learn the Chok Liyisroel and was reminded that Rashi in this weeks Parsha, posuk 20, also brings this verse!). It is interesting to note the connection between the Divine Spirit and the word תרגלתי which has the root meaning feet, thus the verse is talking about the hands and the feet, Rabbainu discusses this in Likutay Moharan explaining that Mordicay is an aspect of the hands the revealed Tora, and Esther an aspect of the feet, the concealed Tora. In this verse our Sages hint to a mercy which is stronger than the great personages of evil that were conjured before Yakov, this is a hint to the last beggar in the Holy Story of the Seven Beggars, the Beggar who doesn't have feet, Rabbi Nachman never revealed his story and it awaits Mushiach coming to be told, this is the power of the feet, as explained in Likutay Moharan Tora 54 the aspect of the Divine in everything in this world. See the Tora there, Rabbainu explains that in order to attain the level of awareness of the feet of Kedusha one needs the power of gathering the winds and melodies in one's hands, this is mamash the succession of the Sixth beggar to the Seventh Beggar! So now you will better appreciate the numerical values going on in this verse. תרגלתי has the numerical value of אני נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן why only one time אני, because H"Y began the verse Himself ואנכי! This is what Rabbainu taught (and it's all over Chazal) that the name of Hashem Y' is shared in the name of the Tzadik! The end of the verse – the do not know that I רפאתים, healed them, the kishkas of this word, פאתי, have the numerical value of נ נח נחמ נחמןן מאומן, and the shell רם, have the numerical value of the shell, klipa, עמלק, who is destroyed by נ נח (see the music site Raanans song, the Jew who killed haman), who's first letters ננננמ have the same numerical value רם – this is as it is written – ראשית – the first – גוים עמלק ואחריתו עדי אובד, at the end of this verse of Hoshaya they are demolished. NNNNM!

posts.title: Good Chodesh! Good Nanach!
posts.body: B"H as SM already pointed out this month - Shevat, is represented by the letter צ which is the Tzadik. Shevat is also a terminology for Tfila (see Likutay Halachos C"M) because Tfila is the staff of the Tzadik and the 12 shivatim are the 12 paths of Tfila. Also the permutation of Hashem's name for this month alludes to tmuros - the switching - which only the Tzadik sees beyond them and overcomes them. My father told me that it is not uncommon for the sefer Or Gedalyahu by R' Gedalya Schorr to quote Likutay Moharan, and he does so regarding the inyan of Rosh Chodesh, and thus my father had (once again) the merit of quoting a Likutay Moharan in one of his shiurim.

posts.title: Nanach is the rectification of Nevuchadnetzar
posts.body: The Talmud in Chalek (the tenth chapter of Tractate Sanhedrin) saysthat נבוכדנצר was capable of singing to Hashem praises that would makethe Psalms pale in comparison. This is a sign that his soul had verydeep roots, and the deeper one's roots the greater is the depths thesoul must subjugate and conquer for the good, but obviously he was notsuccessful (if I recall correctly the sefer Nefesh Hachaim by R. ChaimVolozhin discusses this, or it may be brought up as a question to whathe writes, it is something I discuss in my unpublished commentary tohis work, Simchas Hachaim). What he needed was the ultimate power ofconquering and reversing even the most evil to good – Rabbainu Na NachNachmu Nachman MayUman. Very often נבוכדנצר is called נבוכדראצר – we can break up this nameto find it's roots - נבוך דראצר – confused of retzar – retzar has thenumerical value 491 which is that of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman.נבוכדראצר just couldn't figure out the powerful secret that he sodesperately needed - נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן!

posts.title: Nanach! The guts to be holy!
posts.body: In Parshas VuAira there is a verse (6:19) ועתה שלח העז את מקנך Rash"isays that the word העז means to gather, 'now send out and gather yourherds' this is an amazing application of the word which usually meansstrength and more particularly brazeness. This is very well understoodby the teachings of Rabbainu, as we find by Yosef, אסף ה' את חרפתי,'Hashem gathered my disgrace' in order for one to overcome and rectifydisgrace one needs עזות דקדושה 'holy brazeness', so we see that עזותis means of gathering. Guile brazeness is called עזות מצח if we add a yud, which signifiesthe flux of the Ain Sof B"H (the Non Limited one Blessed He) [this issomething done by the Besht in one of his letters – כל רב בבל ורביבא"י כי ר' זה חכמה, ראשית חכמה, וב' זה בינה, אבל זה בלי נבעיות, וכאשרמוסיפין יו'ד וכו' – זה אינו לשונו ממש אבל קצת קרוב כפי מה שאני זוכר)]then we get עזות נצח the holy brawn of the נחמן (gimatria Netzach).The word בעזות with the letters and inclusive have the numerical valueנ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן!

posts.title: Get out of the slavery! Be Nanach!
posts.body: Our sages taught that the tribe of the Levi didn't have to work forthe Egyptians. It is interesting to note that we don't find anymention of people trying to pretend to be of the Leviites then (onlylater, when there was great honor and power involved to we find thingslike this happening, like with Korach). Wouldn't it be a very simpleeffective way to avoid the slavery? This is further evidence to peoples great misconception of what theslavery of Egypt was. People think that it was about manual labor andthe like. The Zohar says that the slavery was about learning theTalmud ויעבידו אותם בחומר ובלבנים, בחומר זו קל וחומר, ובלבנים זוליבון סוגיות – 'the Egyptions enslaved them with mortar and brick,mortar is Kal Vichomar (logical reasoning and proof) and bricks arethe clarification of logical discussions. The tribe of Levi was notenslaved to this labor of figuring out the problems of the things thatare wrong and evil, they dedicated themselves to pursuing just thepure and holy, praying to G-d and studying His ways of Pure Holiness.To be a Levi meant that one had full and active belief that God is oneand everything. The Levi would not work, he believed that God providessustenance so working would be insanity. Therefore it is easy tounderstand that although everyone had the option of leaving theslavery by joining the tribe of Levi, no one did so, because they weretrapped in the slavery of their own ideology grappling with wrong andevil and couldn't free themselves as the tribe of Levi.

posts.title: The importance of the Nanach swipe
posts.body: Sometimes a person is unable to speak, in such circumastances he must use his hands to sign Nanach with the Nanach swipe. This is something that can be learned from Likutay Halachos (Choshen Mishpat, the laws of collecting debts from orphans 3:9) Rabbi Nussun explains that this was the case in the war Moshe and Yehoshua led against Amalaik Y"S who brought an overwhelming contamination which prevented Moshe Rabbainu from being able to express himself verbally and explain to the Israelites they must subject their hearts to G-d, thus he was left with the only alternative to raise his hands to Hashem so that the Israelites should follow suit.

posts.title: Rabbis Of Falsehood
posts.body: In the Hebrew na-nach.net we just published a parable that Rabbi Nachman gave to explain the Rabbis of Falsehood, the point being that after seeing all the honor bestowed upon them and not seeing any new or hidden conception of G-d and His Tora, they come to the conclusion that it must be that there is no higher perception attained by any of our sages heaven forbid. It's a really cool parable, check it out(you can probably get by with the help of google translate). It is interesting to note that Rabbi Nachman concluded the idea by stating that with their conclusion they violate the Belief in Our Sages. One would think that there are alot worse consequences of having deluded rabbis, both for themselves and their followers, but Rabbi Nachman seems to think that the worst aspect is their belittlement and rejection of the supremacy of Our Sages!

posts.title: German Media Coverage of NaNach!
posts.body: B"H last week we posted a video from youtube of Nanach hafatza on the warfront (http://ca.youtube.com/watch?v=QW0D4HkooK0). The video was posted on the youtube by 'Rauskucker' which means a person who sits on a very high place and looks out into the world - so I got to speaking to him, and much of our conversation can be found in the comments to that video. Part of our discussion was about his profile name and I showed him that it was a very similar concept to that discussed by Zalman Shazar (late President of Israel) on the 200 shekel, and translated and discussed by nanach.net sometime last December (http://www.nanach.net/2008/12/two-hundred-shekel-bill-na-nach-nachmu.html). Rauskucker found these words, as we did, to be extremely remarkable, and you can find them now on his homepage on the youtube! Another great development from my conversation with Rauskucker was finding the where-a-bouts of the German media coverage of Nanach. Some of you might recall a couple of months ago a team of German journalists preparing a video and presentation on Nanach, and then we never heard from them again. Well Rauskucker had not only read and seen the presentation he documented it on his homepage, and he was so kind as to share this information with me! It's mamash Givald! Givald! So here are the links, it's two articles and video. If you go to Google translate and paste the URL into the translate box, and set the languages to German - English, they will translate the whole page for you (the first article very well - except for the fact that they also translate Na Nach as Na after, because Nach is German for after, as is Nuch a Na Nach (another NaNach!), the second article which is a much much better one doesn't get translated as well, but it's good enough to understand what is being said). The video narration is mostly built on the second article.article1: http://www.wdr.de/tv/weltweit/sendungsbeitraege/2008/1016/index.jsparticle2: http://www.daserste.de/weltspiegel/beitrag_dyn~uid,mqq4d68347q4vyu1~cm.aspvideo: WARNING!!! posts.title: יששכר חמור גרם וכו' ויט שכמו לסבל
posts.body: While reading last weeks Parsha (Tora portion) which discusses the tribe of Yissochar I found an amazing hint to the holy Song Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman! Rashi brings from our holy sages that there were 200 members of Yissuchar who were privy to the secret of the Ibur (the secret of Nanach as was explained elsewhere), this really perked my interest because 200 in Hebrew is מאתים which has the numerical value of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman (Rashi does in fact spell מאתים with one yud, unlike the 200 shekel bill, featuring Zalman Shazar and two yuds). So I took closer interest in the verse and discovered that שכמו לסבל (with the words and inclusive) has the numerical value of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman! - There indeed is reward (Yesh Sichar)! Later I was perusing through Rabbainu's holy sefer Likutay Moharan and I was reminded that Rabbainu says explicitly (vol. 2, Tora 8:10): ויט שכמו לסבל - זה בחינת נגינה, בחינת שיר חדש הנ"ל... that these words are actually referring to the New Song, Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman!!!

posts.title: Question on Sipuray Maasiyos - The Ancient Tales
posts.body: In the story of the 'Burger'- merchant and the the Emperor, the son of the merchant, the daughter of the Emperor, and the Emperor himself, are living together on an oasis in middle of nowhere. Rabbainu says in the story that the wood for lighting a fire was the equivelant of what would be considered extremely expensive in civilization (very appropriate for our times as what is going on in the world now, to take off the pressure on Israel and to pave the way to bring Rabbainu to E"Y BB"A). Later in the story however, Rabbainu says that everyday the son of the merchant would search 3 trees for the letter he recieved from his fiance, for there were thousands and thousands of trees. My question is, if there were in fact thousands of trees, why was the wood considered so expensive? Maybe we can say that there was no way to chop down the trees, but this seems kind of lame. ANYONE have a solution?Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman!

posts.title: New Tribe of Nanach!
posts.body: In this weeks Parsha (portion of the Tora) our forefather Yakov tells his son Yosef that before the birth of Binyumin, G-d had promised that He would make from him "a nation and a cogregation of nations", Rashi explains (verse 4) a nation, refers to Binyumin, and a congregation of nations, refers to at least another two, so therefore it must be referring to the division of Yosef to his two sons, Efraim and Menashe, each considered a tribe of itself. This can not be the final explanation, because the division of the Yosef to two tribes is at most the addition of one tribe, so what other nation was G-d referring to in His promise to Yakov? G-d's promise of "a congregation of nations" seems to ensure that this is not just an ordinary nation, but a whole bunch. This seems to be a clear promise to the status of the Nanach! Hashem Yisburach promised Yakov that he would produce, in the future, a nation that was a congregation of nations - Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman - which is the Mother of so many diverse peoples! This is also hinted at the end of the verse (Vayichi verse 4)where G-d is quoted saying that He will make from Yakov these nations and give the children of Yakov that will come after him, Israel as an everlasting acquisition -אחוזת עולם- the letters אחוזת עו - have the numerical value of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman! (leaving לם representing the 70 souls of the House of Jacob, which parallel the 70 nations). For it is now at the end of times when the Jews are in fact in Israel that Na Nach has taken its place at the congregation of nations that G-d has promised!!!! Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman!!!

posts.title: Nanach Dreams
posts.body: The Talmud relates all types of dreams the holy Sages had, and how they even when to apparently gentile interpreters (that needs some verification). This is quite astounding, for these holy Sages were hooked up they even recieved messages from heaven on a regular bases, so were they not on the level discussed by the Arizal and even by the Vilna Gaon that teach how when one goes to sleep he can send his soul to visit and study Tora from different Yeshivos of the Holy Ones in Heaven? Even our Holy Master Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman recounted many awesome dreams that he had and he attributed to being the roots of some of his highest teachings. A possible explanation is that dreams are even higher than one can learn in the Heavenly Yeshivos (also see Ramchal, Yichud Hayira, page 308, the secret of the dream is the connection of ... this is what gave intelligence to the Jews in the desert even though they were sinning ... and understand that the dream extends even to gentiles, because it stands in Unity...). This is why everyone can have a dream, just as Rabbi Nachman explains that Biraishes - The Maamar Hasasum - gives life and maintains even the most evil appearances of this world, so to everyone dreams, but the Dreams of the Holy Ones are mamash like prophecy because they are a direct understanding and connection to the source, where as everyone else dreaming are just gleaning from hidden places. Similar also to the analogy Rabbi Nachman relates in his Holy Ancient Tales, that those at the foot of the mountain can see the top, but once they have started climbing they can no longer see the top until they get there. This is possibly why the Holy Sages decidedly chose to use people from the bottom to concretize the visions they had in their dreams. May we all be blessed to have Nanach dreams. (B"H I have heard a few amazing ones, one of them was the revelation that everytime one says Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman 200 people have a thought of repentence).

posts.title: Rabbi Pinto Nanach
posts.body: There was a holy Nanach living in Jerusalem named Rabbi Pinto OB"M. He had an open Yeshiva for anyone who needed a place, and he often took responsability for people, like signing them out of jail (and even....). He gave tzeduka, not only of his time and talents, but incurred huge debts so as to dole out money needed. He made thousands of stickers that said Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman LIYirushalayim - in hopes of elevating the national consciousness to the importance of seeing Rabbi Nachman in Jerusalem the Leader of Israel. So to sum it all up, he was a very fine Nanach indeed. Rabbi Pinto just passed on to the next world about 2 years ago. On our Hebrew na-nach.net (there's a link on the right side of this site that will take you there) they have posted a video of Rabbi Pinto relating the importance of believing in the Petek and Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman. Rabbi Pinto recounts that once there was a scoffer at the holy shrine of Rabbainu, and he was making jest mocking the holy name Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman! This scoffer was saying things like Kuku Riku etc.. When he finished his jest and turned from the holy shrine, the area where the candles were burning and where his son was, burst into flames! There was no medication around or anyone who had any real knowledge how to treat the burned victim, people came rushing to through water on him etc.. Such is the exact and immediate vengence of a person who detrements Na Nach G"F. posts.title: Permutation of G-d's Name for Teves
posts.body: The month of Teves is represented by the following permutation of G-d nameה -י - ה- ו this is spelled out in the final letters of the verse גדלו לה' אתי' ונרוממה' שמו' יחדיו. If we take the letters preceding the final letters - the final letters representing the final sfira, that is the Kingdom of G-d, and the second to final representing the sfira of His Tzadik - we get the letter תומם, meaning wholesome, with the four letters they would actually spell out תמים, which with the word itself has the same numerical value of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman!

posts.title: 3 Nanachs in a Row!

posts.title: Leaving Egypt and Celebrating Chanuka with Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman!
posts.body: In Maoz Tzur - the song we sing on Chanuka after lighting the Menora – we refer to Egypt as עגלה – בשעבוד מלכות עגלה – the servitude of the kingdom of Eglu – a reference to the verse, עגלה יפיפיה מצרים. In Sipuray Maasiyos we learn the Egypt represents the desire for money which one who is consumed by this desire can only be saved by the גבור – the mighty warrior, who will lead them to partake from the aromatic food which allows them to be sensitive to the stench money has. We can hypothesize that the aromatic food is an aspect of the פסח – Passover sacrifice, which our Sages relate had an overcoming aroma, and it was by means of the Pesach that the Israelites left Egypt. From Egypt , the Israelites went on to receive the Tora. So let us work backwards, the redemption from Egypt, כאשר ישא האומן, and the Tora itself being referred to as אומן as we find many places – והייתי אצלו אומן (from this verse our sages learn that the Tora was created before the world). The Pesach being Nachman – as they both share the same numerical value of 148. גבור – is a clear allusion to נ נח נחמ, which is the doubled (-ב) and (ג -) tripled - גב and adds up to רו, all together forming the word גבור. נ נח, is the rectification of עגלה, as they both share the same numerical value. also 50 (נ) times 58 (נח) = Two thousand 900, Two thousand can be represented by a ב, and 900 = ץ, these spell צב and adjective used frequently with the word עגלה. נ is the fall and servitude. נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן!!!!

posts.body: Shlomo Carlbach used to tell over the story of a chusid he called R' Naftoli, who bartered his shoes for a candle to light on the first night of Chanuka (besides the fact that the ground was freezing, this was ample reason for the cursed ones to kill someone). posts.title: THE MISUNDERSTOOD KINDNESS OF THE FAKE RABBIS
posts.body: People are speaking about this Rabbi and that Rabbi how great they and what they are doing. The Nanach are asking well these great Rabbis are they teaching people about the way of Rabbainu, are they teaching them to be always in the Happiness of Mitzva, are they teaching them the importance of rising and starting the day at midnight which is the most fundamental task of a Jew, are they teaching the critical need to speak to G-d personally? Or are they giving their own advice and thoughts? But, they say, look how great they are look at what they have done.... So here ye what Rabbi Nachman says about all the great deed of kindness and miracles performed by the charlatans. Once a thief broke into a house in the middle of the night. He emptied the house of almost all its contents leaving a few articles behind. The thief then ignited the house sending it up in an inferno of flames. Then the thief rushed into the house and with utter urgency and panic he woke up the Parents and the children and helped rescue them from the house and helped salvage whatever was there. Everyone were overcome by gratitude for the thief for saving their lives and their possessions. The Nanach wanted to kill the thief right then and there! This is the matter of the fake holy rabbis that everyone is in such awe of what they are doing. They are the ones responsible for dire state of the Jews in the exile in the first place! They then help make sure that the world isn't brought down completely, and everyone is so full of gratitude for them!!!? The Nanach say that is SHEKER, so the Nanach say if you want to have mercy on yourself, let alone the entire world, avoid the fake holy charlatans, and join the holy Nanach! Rabbi Nachman also said about the fake rabbis that all the miracles they perform is based on the fact that they draw power from their stagnation on the same level, whereas the real tzadikim are constantly nullifying themselves and their achievements to rise and attain higher levels. Rabbi Nachman also taught that many times it looks like the fake rabbi performed a miracle, and in reality, unbeknown to the observer, a real tzadik decided to intervene and help. These are some of the things you should remember and not be sucked in to the Sheker of society. The main thing is to chant and sing NA NACH NACHMU NACHMAN MAYUMAN!

posts.title: Want to bring the whole world back to G-d?!!!!
posts.body: Likutay Eitzos (gathered advice from Rabbi Nachman, Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman) provides a way to bring the whole world back to GOOD. (under the entry of Hisbodidus, 3rd paragraph, based on Likutay Moharan 31:8,9): This is how to do it:By conversation, by conducting conversation and speaking personally to one's creator, and verbally expressing the yearning, and favorable desires, how he yearns and longs, and quells to leave his bad and to merit to the true good, and he prays and supplicates before Hashem Yisburach for this. By this he produces the good souls from potential to actuality. For by yearning alone the souls are created kinetically, and by speech like that mention above, they are completed and go out from potential to actuality. And through this he will merit to the fruition of his requests, and merits to form the letters of the Tora favorably, and he gives life and sustains everything, and he draws goodness and blessing to all the worlds, and he arouses many souls to repentance by means of the words that he spoke between himself and his creator. Because this concept of yearning and favorable desires and to verbalize them with a full mouth is extremely precious, and everyone must accustom themselves to engage in this a lot every day. And through this it is possible to bring the whole world back to GOOD!So here's a little prayer I composed to summarize the above concepts in a petition and supplication to the Lord:Haylige Rachmim (Holy Merciful One) please give me tremendous רצון, השתוקקות,חפץ,חשק , and כיסופין for you and only you, וזכני (and let me merit) להוציא אותם מכח אל הפועל בדיבור פי (to bring them out from their potential into action by verbalization), to pour out my heart to you in לשון הקודש (the holy tongue) ברוח הקודש (with the holy spirit); so that I (cleanse and polish) מנקה ומזכך my גוף and נשמה. And so that I can make many נשמות קודושות וטהורות; and elevate all the נשמות to (will of desire) רעווא דרעווין; and so that I am מנקד ומצייר (vowel and arrange) all the letters of the תורה – לטובה.The main thing of course is to chant and sing Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman!!!!

Saba said we must not sleep, we must spread the light of Rabbainu: Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman! This can be understood beautifully by the Zohar (and Talmud), which goes on to discuss King Chizkiyahu who said that he was not even capable of singing, so he asked of G-d to do the whole thing, wipe out the enemy, while he slept in his bed. posts.title: Chanuka: Tora 2, Likutay Moharan Tinyana
posts.body: Thank G-d we have the Tora of Rabbainu, nothing comes close....This Tora is mamash almost explicitly about Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!In this Tora Rabbi Nachman discusses the verse ויקרא את שמו נח לאמר זה ינחמנו ממעשנו ומעצבון ידינו a direct reference to his name and to Noah, and he elaborates on the 'fourfold' parts of speech - which is mamash the idea of Na Nach - single, double... quadruple!In a previous post I published about how Chanuka is remarkably the concept of Na Nach Nachmu Nachman MayUman, as they are both about publicizing (especially in the streets and marketplace) the wonders of the Tzadik, and they both employ the method of single, double, triple, and quadruple. You should review that post especially to see the RO"SH quoted who paskens that on the first night one blesses the light of Chanaka: Na Na"ch!The question is how come Chanuka goes on to five, six, seven, and eight, back there I suggested an answer, here based on this amazing Tora from Rabbainu I'm going to try a different approach. Obviously every Tora from Rabbainu incorporates the entire Tora so we can expect that the solution is to be found especially in this Tora.Rabbainu says that for the wholesomeness/perfection and to sustain/uphold the fourfold parts of speech it is necessary to light them up with EMES - truth. So it comes out that there's another single, double, triple, quadruple! So it makes so much sense that on Chanuka we do the single, double, triple, and quadruple - twice. This is why its so important to keep saying Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, to draw more and more Truth and Light into the Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!!! In fact the word mayuman does mean exactly that - from truth (emuna encludes the definition truth)!Rabbi Nachman says that one who masters the fourfold parts of speech is the master of the halacha, we can postulate that the fourfold parts of speech parallel the 4 cubits of halacha, this would make Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman the 4 cubits of halacha, from which one should never leave or look out of.With the help of G-d and with motivation from Aron Blanketstatementstien I will continue commenting on this awesome Tora. Stay in tune.NNNNM!

posts.title: Nanach Halacha - Don't hit children!
posts.body: King Solomon, the wisest of men, wrote not to spare the rod on children. The Rambam in the laws of learning Tora (הלכות תלמוד תורה, ב:ב, ז"ל ומכה אותן המלמד להטיל עליהן אימה. ואינו מכה אותן מכת אויב מוסר אכזרי. לפיכך לא יכה אותן בשוטים ולא במקלות אלא ברצועה קטנה) write, that the teacher shall hit the children to instill in them fear, and he should not hit them as an enemy cruel rebuke, therefore he should not hit them with whips nor with sticks, just with a small strap. This is the verdict of the Shulchan Aruch which brings the Rambam almost verbatim (yore daya 245:10). The Vilna Gaon in a famous letter that he wrote to his family while he set off on an attempt to reach Eretz Yisroel (entitled Ulim Litrufa) writes: “and for cursing and swearing and lying hit them and have no mercy on them what-so-ever, because G-d forbid for the perversion of children the father and mother are extremely punished, even if the parents always reared them with ethics and they didn't accept them – woe to the embarrassment, the pain, and the disgrace in the future world, 'her father she profanes' etc.” Rabbainu has a different way. Once Rabbi Nussun related how he had hit his son for not having behaved appropriately, Rabbi Nachman answered with amazement, how can one hit their child?! From then on it was established in Breslov never to hit children (in Bezenson's new book on Nanach he has stories how the Saba managed this).[Perhaps we can say that Rabbainu's attitude has roots in what the Shulchan Aruch rules (Orach Chaim end of Simon 551) that during the 3 weeks in which we mourn the destruction of the Temple and the Holiness of the Israel, one should not hit his students, it is possible to say that Rabbainu considers the destructed state of Judiasm today as a period like the three weeks of mourning, in which there is no allowance for hitting children and students]. So what are you going to do? Who are you going to follow? While we're on topic of Halacha, did you know that the Shulchan Oruch prohibit sleeping (more than 10 minute intervals) during the day? The Arizal slept, because otherwise he didn't have enough strength. So what do you do? Here's something else, the Shulchan Aruch prohibits all women, married or single, to be teachers to small childrenרמב"ם הלכות ת"ת ב:ד, וכן האשה לא תלמד תינוקות מפני אבותיהן שהן באין אצל הבנים, וגירסת הכסף משנה – וכל אשה לא תלמד וכו', וכגרסתו כן פסק בשולחן ערוך (יו"ד הלכות מלמדים רמה:כא) שכל אשה לא תלמד תינוקות מפני אביהם שמביאים בניהם. Do you know anyone that adheres to that Halacha? Thank G-d the Nanach keep the Shulchan Aruch as Rabbainu wanted! Rabbainu made it clear that we are formost servants to G-d and we follow the True Tzadikim, and we study the Shulchan Aruch and we keep the Halacha. The key point is the True Tzadikim, with them we can be servants to G-d and we have a chance at keeping the halacha, without them we can not know G-d and keeping halacha is comical.Thank G-d for Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!

posts.title: Chanuka is the concept of Na Nach!
posts.body: Chanuka is mamash the concept of Na Nach, to publicize the wonders of the True Tzadik, by lighting the menora for everyone to see, and the most beautiful way of lighting the menora by increasing a light every night, the first night lighting one light, the second night two, etc., also the holy name mentioned in the Petek P'TZ'P'TZ'Y'H is the name of Chanoch which is the root of Chanuka, and so Rabbainu Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman would recieve his chasidim on Chanuka. Even still it is astonishing to find that the R"OSH actually points out this connection. In tractate Megila (daf dalet – 4: umud bais) the R"OSH wrote: "That pertaining to the light of Chanuka, the first night the blessing is Na Na"ch etc."!!!!!!!! (We highly recommend seeing this wonder inside with your own eyes! But if you want to quickly see the original hebrew words – check out the hebrew na-nach.net site, there's a link on the right side). There are those that ask why did the R"OSH stop at Na Nach he should of wrote the whole thing? There's another question, how did the RO"SH merit at all to know about Na Nach, isn't Rabbainu the first person to know and reveal Na Nach? These questions answer one another. Rabbainu said that when a person is studying the holy Tora, the Tora reveals herself to the person and then disappears, the person must be very strong and determined to regain the revelation. So we can say that the RO"SH who was unquestionably a holy tzadik (Rabbainu recommends learning the entire RO"SH every year) was learning about the light of Chanuka with holiness and dveikus, and merited some sort of revelation about the true nature of Chanuka, how it all about revealing the wonderous Tzadik etc., and all the RO"SH was able to retain from this revelation was Na Na"ch so the RO"SH wrote Na Na"ch etc.!!!! Others have asked if Chanuka is all about Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, how come we light 8 times in this fashion, where as Na Nach suffices with 4 times? One possible answer is that until Rabbainu established the revelation of Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman in order to achieve NETZACH – victory, it was necessary to do so by means of the musical 8, as we learn in Sefer Hamidos (strife 37) that to gain victory one should say the psalm "on the eight (chords)" (Psalms 6 and 12 – על השמינית), so Chanuka which is all about Netzach was established with the song of 8, thus the lighting ascending to 8. Rabbainu, who's name has the numerical value of Netzach and demonstrated in many ways his affiliation with Netzach, such as his statement: NITZACHTI VANATZAICH (I have been victorious, and I will be victorious), established the victory song "on Ten" – עלי עשור, building it with 4, 1 and 2 and 3 and 4 =10. May we all be zoche this Chanuka to Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!!!!

posts.title: The two hundred shekel bill: Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!
posts.body: The holy book Blossoms of the Spring which is principally letters from the Saba, the master of the Petek, to the President of Israel, Zalman Shazar OB”M, the latter is the one who named the book after the Yidish name of the Saba: Yisroel Ber Odesser (acronym IbaY – Spring), and he is the one who payed for it's publication, aided and supported the Saba, and attended the Kibutz – Breslov gathering – but was thrown out (by zealots). Shazar merited to be profiled on the highest denomination of the Israeli currency, the 200 Shekel bill. Each bill of the Israeli currency hosts an article on either side, these articles are somewhat absurd discussing irrevelant and inpertinant things. Some of the bills even profile figures with head coverings, but their messages are no better. For example one article discusses how the magen duvid was with the Israelites throughout all it's exiles, and draws no conclusion worth mentioning from this. This is where the 200 shekel bill shines out in strong contradistinction! The 200 shekel bill sporting Zalman Shazar, Saba's friend, without a visible head covering, has an unbelievable strong message. The zionists themselves picked the two articles from all of Shazar's writings, so it is quite a wonder that they found nothing more to suit their fancy than these, which clearly undermine the zionist beliefs! According to the zionists, having the state of Israel is Redemption, yet Shazar is quoted on the 200 shekel bill emphatically stressing the urgency to yearn for the redemption, and the belief that in the next world one will be accountable for this! Shazar is quoted promulgating the incumbent and necessary teaching of Tora to the youth, and leadership of the great Jewish sages! It is a miracle that the zionists chose these articles! On one side of the bill: “Behold it is our issue, the nation of the Hebrews, the nation that understood the biblical statute to meticulously teach one's progeny from it's historical inception. This nation even in it's darkest times knew to guard this asset of compulsary study for all it's youth: Already in the time of Rabbi Shimon Ben Shetach, when there was a regathering from the exile to the Land of Israel, she knew to place teachers for the children in every city and in every town, in all the Galilee and in every province, and she established that any city that didn't have a teacher for the children did not have the status of a city, even in the darkness of her being spread out in exile, and in all her communities, she knew to obligate each community to procure teachers for their children on the account of their members. Rich and poor, childless or with many children, single or otherwise – everyone together must bear the burden of the study of TORA.” On the other side of the bill: “Our predecessors established signs to determine the intrinsic faith of a wholesome Jew, they put it to this fundamental question: Did you anticipate salvation? In other words, not only did you desire or did you hope or believe in it, these are not sufficient, rather did you stand yourself on the wall and with concentration of all faculties and with longing eyes anticipated it, just as as a watchman would lookout at a time of danger searching for salvation to be saved. As the watcher of Safed stood themselves on that high lookout, and seeked and seeked.” The complete wonder of all, is that the hebrew word two hundred has the exact numerical value as that of Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!

posts.title: Nanach has the answers at Yahoo!
posts.body: The following question and answer can be found at yahoo answers:How old was our Master the Holy Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman when he passed away?It was forsure before the age of 40 and at least 38 years.sabaynu Your Answer:According to a post on nanach.net, Nov, 12, 2008, "Born on Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5532, he lived 38 years, 6 months, and 18 days - particularly, was Niftar on the 18th day of the 7th month - 18 Tishrei 5571" But there is some controversy about the exact dates, if I recall correctly they are discussed in the original Breslov books, by R' Aryeh Kaplan, and in a manuscript being prepared for publication by the great Nanach, Yosef Aryeh Levin.As for some of the answers given, first of all I see that 2 people confused the Identity of Our Master Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman with that of his follower Rabbi Israel Dov Odesser, known as the Saba. This is a common yet serious mistake. In fact today at the hebrew site na-nach.net there's a post of a TV interview of the Saba in which they ask him if he considers himself a messenger or spokesman for Rabbi Nachman, and the Saba's response is definite and emphatic, that there is no one capable of so directly representing Rabbi Nachman!Next, I address myself to grandmabonnie, it is very disrespectful to equate anyone to Our Master Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, especially someone so questionable as j.c., besides for what historians know of his true nature, even if we would credit him for all the things the christians credit him, he would still pale and be completely insignifigant when compared to Our Master Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman. Grandmbonnie you say that he died to atone for our sins, Rabbi Nachman lived to atone for our sins!!!!!!! At a very young age Rabbi Nachman prayed and cried to G-d that he should feel other peoples suffering as much as they did themselves. Thus for decades Rabbi Nachman lived bearing unutterable and unfathomable pain - as Rabbi Nachman himself put it - the pain he endured would have been cause enough to drive someone to bite through a tree! This is not taking into account the last years of his life when his body was held in miraculous suspension of life, racked with TB. All the miracles aclaimed to j.c. can easily be performed by a begginer of Kabbala, with the uttering and meditation of readily accessible divine names, and names of angels and demons, even an elementary scholar of the Kabala can far out perform the greatest feats j.c. supposedly accomplished. So it is completely out of place, rediculous, and disrespectful to mention him when we are discussing Our Master Rabbi Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman who all the true sages of Israel (not to mention the gentile scholars who only are knowledgable in the outer intelligence of the 7 maids, mathematics, grammar, etc.) are likened to the husk of garlic, and who's everyday chatter the greatest Kabalists wished to understand in the future world or reward, and who's lessons guide the whole world into the Messianic era.Source(s):nanach.netna-nach.netIsrael Saba (conversations of Rabbi Israel Dov Odesser)Chayay Moharan - The Life of Our Master Rabbi Nachman

posts.title: Miracles by the Righteous
posts.body: This weeks Parsha (weekly portion of the Tora) is Toldos, which begins with the verse, אלה תולדות יצחק בן אברהם אברהם הוליד את יצחק, thes are the offspring of Yitchok the son of Avrohom, Avrohom gave birth to Yitzchok. This verse seems to unneccessarily repeat itself. Rashi explains the verse with a Medrash. The laytzanim of the generation (mockers and scoffers) were saying that Avrohom was with Sara for so many years and never had children from her, and now right after Sara's abduction by Avimelech she gives birth, it must be that it was - G-d forbid - Avimelech who fathered Yitzchok. So G-d made Yitzchok's appearance to be identical to that of Avrohom, so that all that saw Yitzchok said that he must be Avrohom's son. The commentaries question this explanation, what would scoffers gain by declaring Avimelech the father, the main miracle wasn't Avrohom's ability to father children, he had already fathered Yishmael, and it's not such a great wonder if 13 years later he fathers another child. The main miracle was that Sara, who was baren at 90 years old would give birth. So even if the scoffers would say that - G-d forbid - Yitzchok was fathered by Avimelech, they would still have to recognise a tremendous miracle had occured! The Brisker Rav answers that it is true that the laytzunim would have to admit that there was a miracle, their objective was to say that the miracle wasn't done for our holy father Avrohom, but for the low down creep Avimelech! This he says is the nature and intent of the laytzunim. This is one of the strongest reasons to learn the Brisker Rav - because now you will get an insite into those people that say that the Petek was written by a certain laytz. What do they stand to gain, after all the Petek is the greatest miracle of all times - never before was a Tzadik revealed in this holy form: Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, never before was there such a powerfull message of hope spread and an opening of thousands of miracles on a daily basis, and the list goes on and on. So what do the laytzunim want, they want to say that the whole Geula - redemption and all the miracles of the Petek is on their account - G-d forbid! So Saba says Ani Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, and all the Nanach echo him, and anyone open to the truth sees that Nanach is the signature of Rabbainu.

posts.title: Bezenson's take on Ani Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun

Bezenson brings a verse from Chumash Shmos when Hashem tells Moshe that He is going to send an angel to lead the Israelites and they should head and obey the angel adherently, כי שמי בקרבו, because my name is in his midst, Rashi explains that this is an allusion to the angel Mata"t whose name has the numerical value of that of the divine name שד"י, Bezenson then brings down from the kabalistic work קהילת יעקב, that because of this attribute Mata"t has the right and ability to say, I am G-d! Thus Bezenson justifies the reasoning for Saba having said, I am Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman.

posts.title: Simplicity and Straightforwardness
posts.body: Rabbainu made it quite clear that the main way to serve G-d in conducting our lives, is with simplicity and straightforwardness. Rabbainu and his chasidim gave many examples of this, such as the story of the simple man who lived in the times of the Baal Shem Tov, this man did not understand the Hebrew prayers yet he said them diligently with all his heart, he would read the entire Siddur - prayer book - daily. The Baal Shem Tov said that when this man would read the parts of the sidur that referred to Pesach (Passover), in Heaven they made Pesach - and so forth for all the holidays and occasions provided for in the Siddur. Another example given is how Rabbainu himself would read all the daily prayers of the Arizal, published in the Siddur Shaarey Tzion, special prayers for each of the seven days of the week, Rabbainu would read them all in one session!The question is, for a simple person who does not know what he is reading, it is certainly exemplary to pray all of the prayers, but for someone who understands the prayers it would seem incorrect and devious to say prayers designed for one day - that mention that day and play on that particular time - on a different day. Simplicity would be to follow the most direct straight forward approach, for a man who does not understand the prayers and wants to pray as much as possible, simplicity may lead him to say all the prayers, but for a man that understands the matters at hand simplicity would direct him to follow the directions of the prayers.Rabbainu said, questions that are stronger than the answers, should not be asked. However I have presently opted to air this point because it was purposely reiterated by Rabbainu and his Chasidim intending for everyone to follow it, so maybe we are allowed to figure out what exactly it is.The best I can make out, for the time being, is that real simplicity is acknowledgement that one really doesn't know anything, and in this way Rabbainu saw himself simply as a such a person who did not know the prayers yet wanted to pray as much as he could. This is in line with what Rabbainu said and even swore on occasion that he did not know any more than those with him, and that he did not know at all. Rabbainu also said that his not knowing was a bigger novelty than his knowing! Thus there is strong ground to my above conclusion, that the epitome of worship and conduct according to Rabbainu it complete negation of all knowledge, even of the meaning of simple words, concentrating on reaching out to G-d with one's heart and whole being, and doing the most simple good deeds (like giving charity again and again).Further thought in this issue can be developed by examining the ways of the Simpleton in the story of the Simpleton and the Wise Guy. The simpleton is portrayed to be the epitome of simplicity and straightforwardness, thus it is significant how he calls his bread by the many tastes that he experiences - which in itself needs understanding why shouldn't the simple way be satisfied with the simple taste of bread, his Peltz (coat) by the many garments its purpose substitutes, etc..NNNNM!

posts.title: Story of the Simpleton and the Wise guy
posts.body: When the wise guy decides to briden his horizons and see the world, he sets out and arives at his first destination where he decides to stay there and work. The traders he came with, he was told, were very good to be with if not for the fact that they travel to great distances. After experiencing the hard labor the wise guy decides that in fact his original plan in order and he once again set out this time actually travelling the world. The wise guy was indeed wise, and Rabbainu's message seems to steer us away from the path of the wise guy, so maybe it not for us to figure out the wise guy, but since it is Rabbainu's Tora, I will point this out, what was the wise guy thinking about when he dropped his first plans, what was he thinking when he accepted the hard labor (something the simpleton never considered, and something completely unnecessary for someone so smart as the wise guy), and finally how did the hard labor convince him that he was mistaken and should revert to his original plans?NNNNM!

posts.title: Don't despair halachikly, just say Nanach!
posts.body: This week I was davening and learning in a shteibel in Boro Park, at my table there was a guy giving a halach shiur, they were learning about what you make mezonos on and what requires hamotzey, it's pretty complicated stuff classifying and figuring out how different foods are made, and there are many machlokes achronim. So I related to them that while I was still sort of Litvish, before I was Nanach, I was sitting at a Shabbos table and this woman asks her husband what to do as she has a sufek whether or not she made or was required to make a blessing on something or other, so he tells her to say Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman. This really got my blood going, here was a halachic problem to be dealt with, what were they thinking. Now a days I realize that in fact there is no other way. If one has a doubt and doesn't know what to do, definitely do not let this confuse and agitate you (as it is known that sufek – doubt – has the numerical value of Amalek), just say Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman and put your faith with the Tzadik (after all it says, Bruchos Lirosh Tzadik, that is where the blessings are!). Amazingly enough the guy giving the shiur heard me out, but that's all he imagined, he was not accepting – but – he interjected – saying Na Nach is not saying the blessing, the blessing was not said. Exactly, I replied, that's exactly the point, if one can not say the blessing for what ever reason, say Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman! The magid shiur was growing agitated, if there is a doubt whether the blessing saying Na Nach will not take the place of the blessing. This is what I am trying to save you from, I replied, do not despair, just say Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman! The magid shiur dismay was growing, he was losing hope nodding his head no no, as he repeated his consternation. This went on and on. Poor soul, he is deprived of Na Nach! Na Nach reasured him that there was indeed hope, no need for dismay or grief. Just say Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!

posts.title: Blessings of the True Rebbe Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman
posts.body: We learned in Chok Lisroel today from Proverbs (Mishley 3:33) מארת ה' בבית רשע ונוה צדיקים יברך, The curse of Hashem is in the house of the wicked and the dwelling of the righteous is blessed. The last letters of the verse, הצדיקים יברך has the exact numerical value of Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman! What remains to determine if there is a direct allusion in the first part of the verse, we can see that the letters בית רשע, can be regrouped to spell רבי תשע, now תשע can be understood as תש ע, that is the weakening of the eyes an obvious allusion to SHEKER - falsehood, as Rabbainu teaches that falsehood weakens the sight, in this vein the verse in congruent to its beginning מארת - the curse, which Rabbainu also teaches connotation of lack of sight. Now based on a previous post not so long ago we learned that תשע has the numerical value of זו בית לכפירה, a place where the word רבי is used quite freely and inappropriately to say the least.May Hashem Yisburach save us from the Sheker and the Shakrunim, especially from those that tried to steal the Petek. May Hashem Yisburach include us in the blessed dwelling of the True Tzadikim of Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman.Since I mentioned that previous post, there was some confusion that resulted. Rabbainu said that when he was 13 years old he attained the perception of the Baal Shem Tov. Rabbainu said that the Baal Shem Tov was drawing from Bina (not Keser like someone suggested in the comments, although in Kabala sometimes Bina can be referred to as Keser, but from the mixed jargon and terminology of the comment, its author obviously thought to differ from Rabbainu), where as he, Rabbi Nachman was drawing from places enormously higher, now there we're talking Keser, and even higher, much higher (see there inside). Rabbainu said that the Magid of Mezrich, the Baal Shem Tov's student was drawing from Chuchma, but obviously a Chuchma lower than the Bina of that of the Baal Shem Tov. Now the Chuchma of a talmid of the Magid, where would that be coming from? It is absurd to even mention it while talking about Rabbainu who is the רבי the True Rebbe, acronym ראש בני ישראל, not just a master of a thousand (as Rabbainu described the בעל התניא זצ"ל).In the great darkness and confusion of today, our only hope is to know and adhere to Rabbainu Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, that is why we have this web site. The Internet is the epitome of the mayhem and apikursus of the day, and זרח בחשך אור, Hashem Yisburach sends light even into the darkest recesses of heresy. We must stay focused and recognise that this light, Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman is our only hope, and it is sufficient, more than enough to rescue us and take us where we have to go. True there are many cute and sweet Rabbis and movements, they just don't cut the bill, don't risk your life, the lives of Israel, and the welfare of the Shichina on them - G-d forbid. Just Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman.If 100 years ago they would have had the Petek, they would have lost their free will, it is only because we are so trapped in utter depth of galus that even with the Petek we still have to choose the right path. 100 years ago if a person wanted Na Nach, it was not revealed to him, he could cry, shout, scream, and put on a temper tantrum, it would be of no avail. He could pay a million dollars, a billion dollars, and all the money in the world - he would not merit to know, say, and sing Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!It has been said that it is worth it to come down to suffer 80 years of this world just to recite one time Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!Did you say Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman? ...Yes, you really did, well then you have cause and opportunity to dance for the rest of your life!!!

posts.title: Ways of Kiruv
posts.body: Our Father Avrohom and his Rebetzin our Mother Sara were very active saving souls bringing them to the one true G-d. Ous Sages taught that Avruhum was mikarev the men and Sara was mikarev the women, the holy Zohar (brought down in todays Chok Lisroel) relates the amazing way that Avruhum would do his kiruv and hachnusas orchim - welcoming guests - very different than the 'dov dov' version taught to us in school (that Avruhum was like some waiter trying to pump his guests with all their desires) The holy Zohar says that when Avruhum would welcome a guest, the trees the guest stood under would show whether the guests were idol worshippers buy spreading their branches not sheltering them, and immediately a spring would sprout from the ground and Avruhum would know to have his guest purify himself. Rashi points out that Avruhum would have his guest clean his feet first to make sure he was clean of idolatry, and only then would he usher the guest in, where as Lot would do the reverse, for, Rashi points out Lot did not care as much about the idolatry.There is however a great deal for us to learn from Lot, for in other places the Holy Tzadikim point out that Lot represents the ways of Mushiach, Lot gets protection and consideration specifically because from him - from his daughters - comes Moshiach. Thus there is strong ground to say that the way of kiruv at the times of Mushiach is not so much the way of holiness and purity practiced by Avruhum and Sara, but just to reach out in any way possible to help the turtured and sufferring. There is in fact a similarity here to Moshe, who is called in the Zohar Mushiach, for the Mechilta teaches that in order for Moshe to marry Tzipora the daughter of Yisro, Yisro made him swear that his first son would be designated for idol worship, obviously this has to be understood properly and there are many ways to explain it, but however it is explained it remains proven that there was some element in which Moshe Rabbainu looked past the idolatry to bring about a better good.So as the Nanach save the world in a new way, do not judge them by the standards of Avruhum, rather look at them as Moshe Rabbainu and the harbinger of the Moshiach!NNNNM!

posts.title: Black President Will Be Rectified with Na Nach
posts.body: This Shabos Hashem Yisburach blessed me with new deep insight into how the current events that are playing out are run by Rabbainu Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman. Much of what I will be writing with G-d help has already been discussed on Nanach.net so I might be brief, expecting the reader to catch up on his own. Also I must say that every person is precious in G-d's eyes, regardless of their skin color, G-d has blessed me with incredible friends that are black, that does not prevent us from understanding history and current events and analyzing the nuances of color and what they represent. My hope is that no one will take offence, and if offence is taken there probably is something in the person taking offence something to reckon with. Rabbi Nachman is the greatest tzadik, so his name is going to encompass what takes place in the world. The first letter of Nachman is נ, which is called a bent nun, signifying the the 50 fallen levels of impurity. The Nun is followed by a ח, this signifies חכמה, wisdom, putting these two letters together is what Rabbainu does in the first Tora in Likutay Moharan, Rabbainu says that one has to find the wisdom, purpose, and intent in everything, and by doing this he will make a mark, ת-תיו, in peoples hearts so that they will hear him. These two letters also spell נח, Noah, people did not listen to Noah, so something was missing from his name – putting the two letters together, my hypothesis is that Noah was unable to see the wisdom, purpose, and intent in complete destruction, this was manifested specificly after the flood when Noah was unable to come to terms with the holocaust he saw and got drunk, which resulted in his being desecrated by his son חם – Chum. As a result of this Noah cursed Chum and the blacks came into existence. Rabbainu says in Likutay Moharan that black is writing – thus we can say that it is the ת – תיו- that Noach was not able to attain and was desecrated by it. ת in hebrew can be replace with מ, following the code of אי"ק בכ"ר גל"ש דמ"ת! Moses – Moshe Rabbainu, begins where Noach ends, Right after Moshe's birth he is placed in an ark and is discovered by an Egyptian, Rashi at the beginning of Parshas Lech Lichu calls the Egyptians: אנשים שחורים ומכוערים אחיהם של כושים, black and disgusting people the brothers of the Kushites. Eventually Moshe Rabbainu marries a women who the Torah describes as Kushite, even though the commentaries explain that the Tora does not mean this literally, it is clear the Moshe Rabbainu did a Tikun – rectification on the Kushite. Thus we see that where Noach made it only to the level of personal survival from the flood, Moshe Rabbainu took over from there, even rectifying the Kushiites. Following my previous hypothesis, this shows Moshe Rabbainu's ability to see the wisdom, purpose, and intent even in utter destruction, thus Moshe Rabbainu was willing to sacrifice his life and name for sake of Israel. This is the level of complete freedom, because there is nothing that can be feared. Thus Moshe Rabbainu was on the level of asking from G-d for a free present, ואתחנן, מתנת חנם, and he was capable of the ultimate sacrifice of not receiving that gift, not being allowed to enter the Holy Land of Israel. Moshe Rabbainu foresaw this from the onset when G-d asked him to go to Egypt to free the Jews, Moshe said שלח נא ביד תשלח, send now/please in the hand of who you will send, Rashi explains that Moshe Rabbainu told G-d, send the other one who you want to send, for I ultimately am not the one who's going to bring them to the Land and redeem them in the future. Examining Moshe's words שלח – send: נא ביד תשלח, lets put aside the letters אבד, the remaining letters have a numerical value of 798 which is the exact numerical value of נחמן, Nachman (in hebrew there are 22 letters, the last has a value of 400, there are then 5 end letters, which have consecutive values, thus the final Nun, as that of Nachman, has a numerical value of 700), the remaining letters אבד - destruction, signify exactly to what was discussed previously, this is the level of Moshe to see purpose and intent even in destruction, Moshe reached the level of חנם – free, this is the third stage, ג, of נ נח נחמ, thus from the song that is single, א, double – ב, triple – ג, quadruple – ד, of נחמן, that is נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן, what is missing to be sent is אבד (for Moshe himself is ג)! So to wrap it all up, Rabbainu Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, begins his name from that place of complete destruction of נ, the levels of impurity and then introduces the tikun – rectification of נח, even to the extent of נחמ , that is the level of חנם attained by Moshe, where the נ, is followed by חם, the origin of the blacks, and it is here that they are rectified. Thus leading to final Nun which signifies the highest state of the 50 levels of purity. On a more simple level one can see this directly in the name of Rabbainu – Nachman – נחמן – where the name Chum is preceded and succeeded with the Nun. This Shabbos I read from Likutay Halachos a Tora that explains this so forthright it is amazing that the author Rabbi Nussun restrained himself from mentioning Nachman. Check out the Tora – Hilchos Trumos and Maasros, ג:ז, Rabbi Nussun explains the commandment of Truma – which our sages explained to mean give 2 from 100, Rabbi Nussun explains that a Jews heart yearns without constraint and there are two direction, yearning with out end for G-d, which enters the 50th level of purity which is infinite, and which has it's dangers, and yearning for bodily desires, which denegrate to the pit of the 50 levels of impurity, so to hold both of these yearnings in place we are commanded to give 1 of 50 for each = 2 from 100. This is amazingly evidenced in the name Nachman, which has the two 50's at the beginning and the end, and in the middle it has 50 minus 2 – חם. This is clearer in the name נ נח נחמ where נחמ equals 98, two short of 100. Rabbi Nussun also discusses there the code of אי"ק בכ"ר, as well as the מ and ן, representing the giving of the Tora. So it looks to me that having a black president, and a lot of Nanach, is the final step to reaching the final Nun, which is infinite purity and freedom.Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!

posts.title: The Story of the Simpleton and the Wise Guy
posts.body: Rabbainu portrays how the simpleton rises to be the Chief Minister. It's important to note that even still the Simpleton does not achieve the status and capabilities of the Baal Shem. The Simpleton does reach the status that he can summon the Baal Shem to him and that the Baal Shem will gratiate him, yet the Simpleton himself does not have the abilities of the Baal Shem. Rabbi Nachman did teach that there are tzadikim that serve Hashem their entire lives and see no results until the world to come, so certainly our case, where the Simpleton merited to great heights just not to those of the Baal Shem, is understandible. Rabbi Nachman having told the story obviously was setting the morals of conduct and reaction and it shouldn't just be left without contemplation, so I'll try to develop the idea. It is also possible to understand this based on the story of the Baal Shem Tov's knowledge of the passing of the Ohr HaChaim, because upon washing his hands he was enlightened with intentions that only the the Master of the Generation is privy, so he inferred that the Ohr HaChaim must have passed on to the next world. In this way we could say that as long as the Baal Shem was in the world the Simpleton would not be privy and empowered like the Baal Shem. It is also possible that there is a tzadik that so to speak represents Hashem in the world, and there are tzadikim that represent the Jews, this is a very deep concept. There is a different approach, to say that the level of the Baal Shem is lower than the level achieved by the simpleton, this is based on the chasidic idea that the great Tzadikim reached the level of miracle working and surpassed it. Rabbi Nachman equated the miracle worker to that of the treasurer who guards the kings fortunes, and the great tzadikim as the kings advisors who amass the fortunes and help the king conquer and subdue all his enemies. Nonetheless the conotation of Baal Shem seems to imply that he was the real and ruling Tzadik.

posts.title: Revelations
posts.body: Just now I was hanging out in one of my favorite hang outs - Shomer Shabos, so I was learning that the Baal Shem Tov lit up the world with his presence in the year תנח! This is givald to know, because the because the beginning of Likutay Moharan speaks about the Rashbi, and I always was thinking that it would have been appropriate to mention the Baal Shem Tov, well now that we know that the Baal Shem Tov made his grand entrance in תנח, this is exactly how Rabbainu begins his holy book, that the words of the wise are only heard in תנח! )דברי חכמים בנחת נשמעים)There's another thing I saw, that the Baal Shem Tov, to bring peace to a quarrel, once wrote a Kumaya with these letters: י.ש.ב.ש.ב. The holy brothers of Sal. (the publisher of the Shas that we probably should be using) suggested that it is the acronym for יהי שלום בחיליך שלוה בארמנותיך. This led me to the realization that שלום בחיליך - peace in your quarters, has the numerical value of Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman (with the 5 words).This book, Maamar Mordichay (from Slunim) also quoted the Baal Shem Tov saying that he would like to be a believer in everything, even though it says פתי יאמין לכל דבר,(a fool believes everything), however it also says שומר פתאים ה. (Hashem guards the foolish).It's amazing how the worst misnagdim - opposers - if they would only search for the truth - even in their own sources and traditions, they would undoubtedly turn Nanach (Rabbainu has a Tora about this in Likutay Moharan). In fact we have seen it happen, and it's going to become more frequent BH"Y!Here's something else I saw, there was a lady in Tzfas that was sick, she dreamed that she should go to the Baal Shem Tov's tzion and she would be healed, she said how's that possible, and was told that the angels had brought the Baal Shem Tov to burial right beside the Arizal (this is consistent with what is taught in the Zohar), so the lady went to pray there, and was healed.We know that the Baal Shem Tov was present by his tzion (Rabbainu used to visit him every night, and later Rebbe Buroch complained that the Baal Shem Tov wasn't there and was to be found by Rabbainu), nonetheless according to the Zohar and this story many aspects of the Baal Shem Tov were brought to Eretz Yisroel.Where's the best place to be with Rabbainu now? My bet is that until Rabbainu is officially allotted his own tzion in Har Tzion, he is mainly to found with the Saba! Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!

posts.title: Lech Lichu
posts.body: Thank G-d Nanach is growing exponentially as can be seen by the tremendous increase of posting and participation on nanach.net (just now in Boro Park a frum lady asked me if I'm from nanach.net and thanked us). Lech Lichu לך לך, each of these words has the numerical value of 50 - נ, the vowels of Lichu have a numerical value greater than Lech of 8 - ח (that is 6 plus the two words) this is an allusion to נ נח Na Nach! When I was a kabalist wrestling with the ideas and notions of the Saba and Nanach, before the publication of the incredible book Yisroel Saba, I had some discussions and debates with the Nanach, I raised the issue of the ways of the Saba which sometimes did not appear to be classical tmimus and pshitus (simplicity and straight forwardness). At the conclusion of one debate I stated that if the Saba's way is the true authentic way of Rabbi Nachman, it can only be that of the way of Rabbi Nachman on his way to Eretz Yisroel! The next time I met with that particular Nanach, he told me that he had thought a great deal about my comment and he thinks that I hit it on the nail - the way of the Saba, the way of the Nanach - is the way to Eretz Yisroel! Prior to Rabbainu's trip to Eretz Yisroel he said that it was inevitable, for his thoughts and conscious were already there. Rabbainu sacrificed his life thousands of times to make it to Israel (as written by Rabbi Nussun), and had no mercy on his family and other dependents, not letting them stop or hinder him. This Mesiras Nefesh is fundamental to the way of the Nanach, but there is something much more telling of the way of the Nanach. Before Rabbi Nachman travelled to Eretz Yisroel it was an extremely difficult and dangerous journey. Afterwards Rabbi Nachman said that now anyone can travel with ease. In 1922 the time had come for the Jews to really start going to Israel, unfortunately we were only zoche to realize this much later as the Saba wrote to the President of Israel Zalman Shazar, and it took 60 years till we meritted to the actual way to Eretz Yisroel through which every Jew can merit to get to Israel. Rabbainu hid himself and his avoday - devotion, as a child (that included at least the first 5 years of his married life) he would spend a lot of time playing children's games, running around in the street etc.. Even after he revealed himself as a Chasidic Master, and even after he revealed himself to be the Leading Master of his generation and of all times, Rabbi Nachman hid most of his identity. On his journey to Eretz Yisroel (apx. his age to be 26) Rabbi Nachman conducted himself as a child, playing war games in the streets, dancing, jumping, and hopping and doing all types of antics. These he said made it possible for him to reach Eretz Yisroel. Rabbi Nachman said that such great tzadikim as the Baal Shem Tove weren't able to do this avoda, and consequently they were not able to make it Eretz Yisroel. This incredible avoda, which on the one hand stoops to quite unruly conduct cuts down the opposition of the evil and transforms everything to good, showing the way to Eretz Yisroel, the place where Rabbi Nachman merited to be completely good (that is no matter what a person would do to him he would only see it as an act of goodness). Saba spoke a lot about the importance of coming to Eretz Yisroel, and he encouraged everyone to do so. There is a long chapter in Yisroel Saba where the Saba extols Eretz Yisroel and the importance of being there. Also in the book Chayay Yisroel there are many stories of how Saba convinced and helped people to move to Eretz Yisroel. Rabbi Nachman said that to be a Jew, that is to constantly rise, one must be in Eretz Yisrael. Getting to Eretz Yisrael is a journey is in itself an introduction to the journey that takes place in Eretz Yisroel. The Ramchal points out that most of the secrets of the Zohar are recounted while their masters were traveling. We must begin this journey now - the way of the Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman, from Uman to G-d only know where. Rabbi Nachman said (intro. to Likutay Moharan 2) that in order for a person to properly worship G-d he must be like Father Avrohom who stood up against the whole world, One against the whole world. Rash"i says that on Avruhom's journey he had to borrow money, which he later paid back after Hashem Yisburach blessed him with money. This means that initially Avrohom Uvinu, not only did he fight against the whole world, but while fighting them he had to borrow money from them! So we see that whatever the cost is, dancing in the streets or borrowing money, it is well worth it to get to Eretz Yisroel. This was one of the ten tests of Avrohom Uvinu. Can you make it to Eretz Yisroel? Can you sing Nanach and dance in the streets?!Na Nach Nachmu Nachmun MayUman!

posts.title: Shulchan Aruch - Law
posts.body: This is the 231 statute of the Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim:That all his intentions should be for the sake of heaven:If it impossible to learn without sleeping in the noon, he should sleep. Only he should not extend it, for it forbidden to sleep in the day more than the sleep of a horse which is 60 breaths (the K. Rebbe told me this is about 10 minutes). And even in this little amount his intention should not be to pleasure his body, but to strengthen his body for the service of Hashem Yisborach. And so in everything that he enjoys in this world, he should not intend for his pleasure, but for the service of the Creator Yisborach, as it says (Proverbs - Mishley 3:6) "In all your ways know Him", and our sages said: "all your actions should be for the sake of heaven", that even regular permissible things, such a eating, and drinking, and walking, and sitting, and rising, and intercourse, and speaking, and all necessities of the body, they should all be for the service of your creator, or for something that will lead to His service. That even if he is thirsty or starving, if he eats or drinks for his pleasure this is not commended, rather his intentions should be to eat and drink for the amount required to live, to serve his creator. And this is so even regarding sitting in the privy of the righteous, and the standing in the presence of the tzadikim, and the travel in the scheme of the wholesome, if he does so for his own pleasure to fulfill his desire and urges of pleasure, he is not commended' only if he does so for the sake of heaven. And so with resting, it is not necessary to talk about the time when he can be involved in the Tora and Mitzvos - he should not provoke with sleeping to pleasure himself, but even at times when he is exhausted and must sleep in order to rest from his efforts, if he does so for the pleasure of his body he is not commended, rather he should intend to give sleep to his eyes and rest to his body in order to be healthy, so that he should not confound his Tora intellect from lack of sleep. And so in the matter of .... And so in conversation, even to relate matters of wisdom his intentions must be for the service of the Creator or for something that will lead to His service. The Principle of the matter is, everyone is obligated to be concentrate his eyes and heart on his ways and to measure all his actions with the scales of his intellect, and when he sees something that can bring service to the Creator Yisborach he should do it, and if not he should not do it. And whoever practices this, he is serving the Creator always.

posts.title: Saba's Yartzheit (anniversary of death)
posts.body: There has been some posting about Nanach being the Tikun - rectification - of the flood. So here's some more to let your brain chew on. According to R' Eliezer the flood started with rain of blessing (as Rashi says, Hashem made it so that the rain would be just of blessing, but since they were obstinate in sin the rain turned into the flood) on the 17th of Cheshvon, Rashi (in today's chok) points out that since it didn't start from the night (which is in most cases the beginning of the day) therefore the 17th is not considered in the 40 days of rain that the Tora talks of. This means that in many aspects the actual start of the rain is 18 Cheshvon - the Yartzheit of Saba! Also previously Rashi (on the verse (in seven more days) says that the flood was postponed for the 7 days of mourning honoring the death of Misushelach - which could technicly place his death on the 9th of Cheshvon - the Yartzheit of R' Yisroel Karduner - Saba's mentor.
